name: FastestJSONInTheWest
workload: End-to-end parse of small/medium/large JSON payloads (162B-1MB), plus post-parse field access, array iteration over 10K records, and on-demand single-field extraction from a 1MB payload, via Google Benchmark.
claimed_speedup: Loses badly on raw parse (simdjson is 46x-116x faster, e.g. 83-112 MB/s vs 4.1-11.1 GB/s); wins on pre-parsed field access (1.26x) and array iteration (2.24x); its own on-demand mode is 7.8x faster than its own full parse for single-field extraction, but this is a self-comparison, not a win over simdjson's ondemand mode
tradeoffs: Raw parse throughput is 46x-116x slower than simdjson; the claimed wins are limited to secondary access patterns on an already-built DOM (repeated field access, array iteration) rather than parse-from-bytes speed, which is the primary thing simdjson is used for; also supports read-write serialization which simdjson does not, so that part of the comparison isn't head-to-head.
caveats: Solo, unverified project with 0 stars and a very sprawling repo layout (Bazel, ai/, python bindings, many top-level docs) consistent with heavy AI-assisted authoring; GitHub reports the license as 'Other'/NOASSERTION and a LICENSE_BSD_4_CLAUSE file exists but a direct raw-content fetch of a LICENSE file 404'd, so exact terms are unconfirmed (treated as non-OSI/reference); the project's own name overstates the result, since on its core job (parsing from bytes) it is dramatically slower than simdjson; numbers are entirely self-reported with no independent reproduction found.
found_via: Blogs / talks: gh search code "faster than simdjson" -> oldboldpilot/fastestjsoninthewest docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md

verification.tier_reason: First-party Google Benchmark code is public (benchmarks/fastjson_vs_simdjson.cpp, linked against real simdjson). The v3.0 results state Clang 21, C++23, 'Linux x86_64, 32 cores, 2995 MHz', but give no CPU model and no flags for that run (only the legacy section says -O3). That falls short of A, so C.
verification.notes: Rejected as not-faster on real-invalidity grounds, not scope. It loses every like-for-like comparison with simdjson. Its only 'wins' exclude its own parse cost from the timed loop, and its older 'faster than simdjson' table benchmarks a sleep_for simulator. If the orchestrator keeps it under the flagged-entry policy, the corrected claimed_speedup and caveats document the shortcomings. Metadata verified via gh: not fork or archived, 0 stars, last commit 2026-08-15 (active), license file is BSD-4-Clause.
